name: needs-collapse-visual
description: Visual check of collapse state: dispatch an employee to work so need gauges drain at the working rate and no rest can be claimed, drive fatigue below the collapse threshold (≤5), verify the employee is flagged COLLAPSING in state and rendered with the collapsing row style, then build living_quarters and advance ticks to confirm rest recovery and a return to normal task dispatch

steps.description: cash:100000, not the $50,000 default: a genuine, pre-existing bug (Finding, whole-suite scenario audit) -- this file hires 2 employees and runs 300 ticks of continuous payroll with zero income anywhere in it, and the default $50,000 start goes to exactly -$10,950 by the time the build living_quarters step below runs, correctly disabling its buy button on insufficient funds (a real gate, not a stale-UI artifact -- confirmed by direct diagnosis: reordering the build to run before the ticks avoids the shortfall but breaks something else entirely, the employee's natural fatigue recovery no longer completing by tick 200 (collapsedCount stays 1 instead of returning to 0) -- so the fix is more starting cash, not a different step order. $100,000 leaves $38,950 at the build step, a comfortable margin above its $10,000 cost.

Left unmarked: no UI control drives this exact command and none should exist -- employees.ts's own `dispatch` case comment: "no console command currently creates one... which left the Bunkhouse shift-cycle unreachable from any player-facing flow" -- a test hook by design, same class as `employee assign_skill`.

Added for #547. Queued now, second in line behind the first dispatch, this claims the instant the first completes -- ahead of any auto-inserted rest, which only gets queued once fatigue crosses its warning threshold near the end of the first task and so always lands later in pendingActions. Before #547, a null-skill dispatch never seeded pendingTaskDuration, so the single original dispatch here never completed and Walt stayed 'busy' (and undisturbable by his own proactive rest) forever -- which is what let fatigue drain straight through to collapse under the old calibration. #547 fixed that leak, so a lone dispatch now genuinely completes and frees Walt to be routed to rest before he ever reaches the collapse floor (see needs-proactive-queue-visual's equivalent note). This second dispatch keeps him continuously working across the handoff, restoring the file's own premise ("no rest can be claimed") instead of the accidental one the old bug provided.

#680 follow-up: Stan (id 2, blaster), like Walt, must be genuinely, continuously busy for his own later collapse checkpoint to stay reachable — autoInsertNeedTasks now auto-routes ANY fully idle employee (with or without a living_quarters anywhere on the map) into a same-tick, zero-distance, zero-drain ground-rest the instant a gauge dips under its warning threshold, so an employee left idle the whole file can no longer collapse at all (direct probe, GameLoop.ts). A busy employee's queued rest stays unclaimed instead, so genuine neglect (no idle window, no living_quarters yet) still bites. Repeated ahead of each tick block below to keep him continuously dispatched the same way Walt is, right up to the collapse checkpoint (#593's note, below, on why it's specifically Stan's crossing).

A third hire, brought on purely to build the quarters ordered below (#556). Neither Walter nor Stan can: this file works both of them to exhaustion on purpose, and an employee deep in the collapse cycle never claims a construction site. Hired fresh immediately before the order so it is nowhere near its own collapse threshold during the push below — and so the quarters gets built without Walter leaving the rest-in-place he would otherwise hold, which an earlier order cost in an extra collapse this file asserts against on every step.

expect.note: Ordering only queues a construction site (#556). The fresh hire above builds it across the collapse push below and the closing wait; the standing building is asserted there, not here.

expect.note: #700 follow-up: replenishment now applies its rate for a rest's own full duration, so a completed rest recovers much more than before -- keeping Stan continuously re-dispatched every 5 ticks (rather than the old single 20/30-tick gaps) closes the idle window an auto-claimed rest could otherwise slip into and recover him. Under this tighter cadence he still crosses the collapse threshold from continuous working-rate drain with no rest ever claimed (a real run confirms 'NEED: employee_collapsed' fires within this final batch). This is the collapsing-row visual checkpoint (see 'collapse-state' shot).
